facts.fact: 夏末城市空了，但城里的死者越来越吵。
facts.anchor: It was the end of summer and the city felt empty. But the city’s dead were getting louder.

facts.fact: Bowery 某处：她看见女人从窗口跳下、却在落地前消失；Julie 解释——CBGB 对面的百年妓院。
facts.anchor: There’s a spot on the Bowery where I saw women hurl themselves out the window but disappear before they hit the ground. I asked Julie, and of course she knew all about it: “Across from CBGBs? Notorious brothel a hundred years ago.”

facts.fact: 她怕的是那些女孩在最不想待的地方醒来，别无逃法，只好反复重演那以为能结束一切的一跃。
facts.anchor: It spooked me to think of girls’ waking up in the last place they wanted to be and, not knowing how else to escape, reliving the long dive they thought would end it all.

facts.fact: A 街上一个焦裙、头发湿透的女人用德语问她孩子在哪——她听得懂，因为像意第绪语，而她自己都不知道自己会。
facts.anchor: On Avenue A, a woman in a scorched dress and, somehow, soaking-wet hair asked me in German where her child was. (I could only understand because it sounded like Yiddish, which I didn’t even know I knew.)

facts.fact: 另一个长发及臀、披鸟羽外套的女人沿百老汇跟了她好几个街区。
facts.anchor: Another woman, with black hair down to her hips and a coat made of bird feathers, followed me for blocks up Broadway.

facts.fact: 要穿城必须绕开华盛顿广场公园，否则会看见男人吊在树上、女人咳出烟。
facts.anchor: I had to entirely avoid Washington Square Park if I wanted to cross town without seeing men swing from trees or women cough up smoke.

facts.fact: 她可以移开视线却躲不开身体落地声——不像她以为的，像一筐衣服从窗口扔出。
facts.anchor: I could look away, but I couldn’t avoid the sound of bodies hitting the pavement, which doesn’t sound like what you think. It sounds like a pile of laundry tossed out the window.

facts.fact: 新声音：无来处的尖叫、转角处的低语，你一出现就停，像在议论你。
facts.anchor: The sounds were new to me: screams from nowhere, whispers around the corner that stopped when you turned up, as if they were talking about you.

facts.fact: 她凭记忆画失去的人的脸却总不相像——问题出在画眼睛时：她看不见他们所见，因此看不见他们。
facts.anchor: I tried drawing faces from memory, people I knew and had lost, but their likeness evaded me just when I tried filling out their eyes. I couldn’t see what they saw, and so I couldn’t see them.

facts.fact: 她只想让「Mark 死去的那个夏天」结束，它却拖到九月。
facts.anchor: I was ready for The Summer Mark Died to be over, but it stretched well into September.

facts.fact: 她反复听《Heaven》：那个小艺术呆子说得对——天堂是个所有人泡着、什么都不发生的酒吧。
facts.anchor: I kept going back and playing “Heaven” because I thought that little art nerd was right that heaven was a bar where everyone hung out and nothing ever happened.

facts.fact: 她去看 Star，警察没去；打死 Michael Stewart 的警察案子被撤销。
facts.anchor: I visited Star, the cops did not. The cops who beat Michael Stewart to death had their case dismissed.

facts.fact: 她想 Claude：想念一个还在、还能轻易说话的人显得愚蠢——可那并不容易。
facts.anchor: I thought about Claude. It felt stupid to miss someone who was still around, whom I could talk to easily, but it didn’t feel easy.
